text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliamentarians agree on importance of MP representation in post-election government but not on number. Parliament polls were held last week. By law, the new government must include at least one elected MP.
- Strict laws and high fees drive foreign investments away from Kuwait to neighbouring states, economic experts say.
- Kuwait concerned over Iraq's delay in paying compensation for damages caused by the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
- Kuwait Investment Projets Company purchases 15.5 million shares of Burgan Bank raising its stake to 22 percent.
- Communications ministry warns 11,000 subscribers to pay telephone bills.
- British foreign office minister Hanley says Iraq's Saddam Hussein remains a threat. Hanley arrived in Kuwaiti on Monday night.
- Prime minister continues consultations with MPs to form new government.
